acceptanceCriteria: JT-AC-034: failures, conflicting events, malformed data, and rapid operations resolve through deterministic state transitions without corrupting unrelated valid data.
JT-TEST-144, JT-TEST-145, and JT-TEST-146 cover subsystem failure containment, exhaustive playback-state transitions, and concurrent persistence responsiveness.
Failure, interruption, route change, and recovery preserve stopped playback until an explicit permitted user restart.
notes: Planning complete for the deterministic failure-containment portion of SP-016. File an Issue for observed approved-requirement violations; do not expand recovery behavior or feature scope without explicit authorization.
Keep deterministic failure-injection output, simulator inspection, and physical-device or listening evidence separate. A simulator cannot establish audible recovery or route behavior.
rationale: Deterministic stopped playback, data integrity, and UI responsiveness are cross-platform release-critical reliability behavior.
testSteps: Run JT-TEST-144 by injecting or simulating failures in audio rendering, Watch synchronization, catalog loading, import processing, and persistence; record recovery, data-integrity, and usability outcomes.

Run JT-TEST-145 against user actions, interruption, route change, engine failure, backgrounding, and cross-device updates, including conflicting or rapid event orderings; assert no unexpected playback or implicit restart.

Run JT-TEST-146 with rapid consecutive valid edits during playback; record primary-screen and audio responsiveness, then reload persisted state to verify the latest complete acknowledged edit is durable.
Record build or commit, platform, device and OS where used, route, starting state, exact event sequence, observed result, and whether evidence is automated, simulator, or physical device.

workItem.title: Qualify deterministic failure containment and responsiveness
